subject: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan

Team —

After the last two months of performance calibrations and throughput analysis, I want to propose a targeted consolidation of two manager roles across the Serving Runtime org (Eng Pods B3/B4). The high-level rationale: reducing one layer where scope overlap is creating operational lag, and simplifying on-call/feature ownership.

Key elements of the proposal (attached: proposed_org_charts_v2.pdf):
- Merge Manager B3 and Manager B4 into a single Director-facing manager (pilot for 90 days).
- Reassign two senior ICs to lead technical ownership of their former areas instead of a replacement manager hire.
- Offer a short-term review exception for impacted contributors: shift their annual rating window + provide clear SUCCESS criteria for the transition.

Risks & mitigation I want us to consider:
- Morale and perception: need tight comms and manager 1:1s (draft comms attached).
- Compensation delta: comp_impact_model.xlsx models 3 options (retain T-level comp, short duration retention stipend, or targeted bonus).
- HR/legal: must pre-clear any involuntary changes and document alternatives (re-scope, lateral moves).

Requesting:
1) Quick alignment from Laura and Marcus on org impact and delivery risk (are there active hiring offers that would be affected?).
2) HR (Neha) to confirm required approvals and minimum timeline steps if we move forward.
3) Hannah — input on manager bandwidth and on-call rotation impact.

I propose a 30-minute calibration on Monday (Apr 12) to decide whether to pilot this in B3/B4 or rework the plan.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan

Vivek —

Thanks for the thoughtful write-up. A few immediate notes from talent and product continuity perspective:

1) Active offers: We currently have two open offers for ICs in B4 (both pending sign) and one internal candidate considering a manager lateral. Cancelling or re-routing those offers will affect our hiring funnel and time-to-fill metrics. Suggest we freeze new external offers for 72 hours while we decide.

2) Review exceptions: Any shift in rating windows must be explicit in the calibration notes. People moved to a different role during the review cycle will need a written success plan (approx 60–90 days) and a communication that this is not an immediate performance action.

3) Comms: The draft in comms_draft_for_managers.docx is a good start but we should add a short FAQ for ICs covering severance, lateral options, and impact to career ladder.

I'm concerned about concentrating too many direct reports under one manager in the short term — that may create a gap in career coaching. If we pilot, please commit to an evaluation checkpoint at 30 and 60 days with clear metrics (support tickets escalated, PR review turnaround, on-call incident MTTD).

Happy to discuss on Monday.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan

Vivek / Laura —

I appreciate the lean approach. A slightly different operational idea: rather than immediately consolidating manager roles, can we trial a matrix lead model for 60 days? That keeps manager headcount but shifts day-to-day ownership to senior IC leads (reduced management bandwidth required) and gives us more runway to observe effects on throughput.

On the compensation side, I'd prefer the short-duration retention stipend (option 2 in the spreadsheet) to avoid creating long-term comp policy exceptions. Also, for hiring: we should convert one external offer to a short-term contract to preserve capacity.

If HR can confirm the paperwork steps, I'm supportive of a pilot with measurement gates.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan

Thanks for the ping — couple of HR guardrails and process notes: 

1) Any role consolidation that changes reporting lines but is not a reduction in force is generally handled as a "re-scope". We need documented consent from the impacted employee for scope change when it materially changes duties. We should prepare at least two written role descriptions (old and new) for affected folks.

2) Review exceptions are allowed, but we must record them in Workday as an "exception note" and notify Total Rewards. If we shift someone's review window, that must be reflected in compensation runbooks. That adds ~5 business days of admin overhead.

3) If we consider involuntary moves, we need Legal looped and 30 days' notice or equivalent compensation per policy. Recommend we avoid involuntary moves wherever possible.

4) Comms framing: managers should lead 1:1s this week using the attached manager script (I included suggested language at the top of comms_draft_for_managers.docx). We should also give ICs a dedicated Q&A doc and an anonymous channel for feedback for 10 business days.

Operationally, I support Marcus' matrix approach as a lower-risk pilot path. If leadership wants consolidation after the pilot, HR will need a signed acceptance form from impacted employees for role scope changes.

I'll be available in calibration but also happy to run a quick checklist after the meeting so we don't miss gating items.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior HR Business Partner

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: managerial layer consolidation + review exception plan — decision and next steps

Appreciate the fast feedback — summary & decisions from today's calibration: 

1) Pilot approach: we will run Marcus' matrix lead pilot for 60 days in Pods B3/B4 starting Monday Apr 26. No immediate manager headcount reduction.
2) Hiring: freeze external offers for 72 hours as Laura suggested; convert one offer into a 3-month contract for capacity continuity. HR to confirm the vendor pathway.
3) Reviews & comp: adopt the short-duration retention stipend approach (comp_impact_model.xlsx, option 2) for individuals who take on expanded responsibilities. HR to record review exceptions and update Workday.
4) Comms: Hannah & Laura to finalize manager scripts and an FAQ by Apr 22; Neha will publish the anonymous feedback channel.
5) Measurement: 30/60 day gates with success criteria (support ticket escalations, PR review latency, on-call MTTD). Marcus will own the metrics dashboard; Vivek will review at the 30-day checkpoint.

Attachments: proposed_org_charts_v2.pdf, comp_impact_model.xlsx, comms_draft_for_managers.docx

I'll draft the manager email and share before EOD tomorrow. Thanks for the fast turn.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference
